questions.cardText:
[History] Where is the Japanese dish “tempura” originally from?
A. Portugal B. Britain C. China
Answer: A. The Japanese dish “tempura” was introduced by the Portuguese travelers in the 16th century. It was adapted from a battered and fried green bean recipe called peixinhos da horta.
questions.de: Aus welchem Land stammt das japanische Gericht Tempura ursprünglich – im 16. Jahrhundert von Reisenden gebracht und aus frittierten grünen Bohnen namens peixinhos da horta abgeleitet?
questions.en: From which country did the Japanese dish tempura originally come, brought by travellers in the 16th century and adapted from fried green beans called peixinhos da horta?

timeline.labelEn: Portuguese Jesuits and traders bring battered frying to Japan via the Nanban trade, origin of tempura
timeline.labelDe: Portugiesische Jesuiten und Händler bringen über den Nanban-Handel das Frittieren im Teigmantel nach Japan – Ursprung des Tempura

questions.notes: Wikipedia credits Portuguese Jesuits via the Nanban trade; peixinhos da horta is named as tempura's Portuguese ancestor.

questions.cardText:
[Zoology] Which of the following actions can a leech perform?
A. Jumping
B. Flying
C. Running
Answer: A. Recent research has provided video evidence that some terrestrial leeches can jump. In a 2023 expedition, leeches were seen recoiling their bodies before launching into the air. Understanding the mechanics of leech jumping could inspire the development of more adaptable robots.
questions.de: Welche lange bezweifelte Fortbewegung mancher Landblutegel wurde durch eine 2024 veröffentlichte Studie in Madagaskar auf Video belegt?
questions.en: Which movement of some terrestrial leeches, long doubted, was proved on video in Madagascar by a study published in 2024?

timeline.labelEn: Mai Fahmy and Michael Tessler publish the first proof that a terrestrial leech (Chtonobdella fallax) jumps
timeline.labelDe: Mai Fahmy und Michael Tessler veröffentlichen den ersten Beleg, dass ein Landblutegel (Chtonobdella fallax) springt

source.title: First conclusive evidence that a terrestrial leech species can jump

questions.notes: Card is right: filmed on expeditions to Madagascar in 2017 and 2023; paper "A jumping terrestrial leech from Madagascar", Biotropica, 20 June 2024.
